observations: Torah #95 is a brief practical instruction (five sentences) on hitbodedut — personal prayer and meditation before God. The teaching contains only one explicit bechina equivalence: ציפייה לבכיה (the anticipation/expectation of weeping during prayer) is declared a bechina of מחשבה זרה (alien thought that confuses kavvanah). This constitutes only two concepts — far below the threshold of 3+ bechina-connected concepts required to form an independent domain and propose a new package. The remaining conceptual vocabulary of the Torah — דיבור (speaking), בכיה (weeping), לב שלם (wholeness of heart), כוונה (intent), and the metaphor of speaking as a man to his friend — are all mentioned in an eitza (cause-and-effect) frame: focus on the words → heart awakens → true weeping. They do not form bechina clusters. Therefore no new packages are proposed. If the dataset were to be enriched with the missing bechina pair (ציפייה לבכיה ↔ מחשבה זרה), it would yield one minimal two-node package of evil/obstruction polarity centered on מחשבה זרה, but this still would not reach the threshold for a new-package proposal as defined by the algorithm.
